notes.text: Drop the ーます from the ーます form and add なさい to make this form.
notes.html: Drop the ーます from the ーます form and add なさい to make this form.

examples.japanese: 「一人で間違えずに歌える自信のある人だけ座りなさい。」と指示しました
examples.body_text:
「一人で間違えずに歌える自信のある人だけ座りなさい。」と指示しました 

		[The teacher] directed that (just) people who had the confidence that they could sing, on their own, without error 
		should 
		sit down.
examples.body_html:
「一人で間違えずに歌える自信のある人だけ座りなさい。」と指示しました 
[The teacher] directed that (just) people who had the confidence that they could sing, on their own, without error should sit down.

examples.body_text:
早くしなさい。 

Do it 
		quickly.
examples.body_html:
早くしなさい。 
Do it quickly.

examples.japanese: 好い加減にしなさいよ。
examples.body_text:
好い加減にしなさいよ。 

Shape up!
examples.body_html:
好い加減にしなさいよ。 
Shape up!

examples.body_text:
野菜を食べなさい！ 

		Eat your vegetables!
examples.body_html:
野菜を食べなさい！  
Eat your vegetables!

座りなさい。 
Sit down.

comments.text: I guess this is half way between a 'polite command' and a 'fairly forceful request'.
comments.html: I guess this is half way between a 'polite command' and a 'fairly forceful request'.

comments.text:
'[The teacher]' isn't explicitly in the Japanese version, but the English might look odd without it.



'(just)' wouldn't be natural in the English - the だけ in the Japanese doesn't explicitly tranlate.
comments.html:
'[The teacher]' isn't explicitly in the Japanese version, but the English might look odd without it.

'(just)' wouldn't be natural in the English - the だけ in the Japanese doesn't explicitly tranlate.

comments.text:
The Japanese translation is quite nice except the tense.

「…。」と、（先生は）指示しました／指示した。
comments.html:
The Japanese translation is quite nice except the tense.
「…。」と、（先生は）指示しました／指示した。

comments.text:
In the English version of the first example, perhaps "just those" instead of "(just) people." 

Also, I don't know how they do it in schools abroad, but in Japan, the teacher normally says "should stand up" instead of "should sit down."
comments.html:
In the English version of the first example, perhaps "just those" instead of "(just) people."
Also, I don't know how they do it in schools abroad, but in Japan, the teacher normally says "should stand up" instead of "should sit down."

related_entries.label: na-3
related_entries.annotation_text: na-3    (The command form な is based on the request form なさい (or similar). な is much more forceful.) [Amatuka]
related_entries.annotation_html: na-3    (The command form な is based on the request form なさい (or similar). な is much more forceful.) [Amatuka]

related_entries.label: kudasai
related_entries.annotation_text: kudasai    (なさい and ください can both be used to make requests, although なさい is probably more forceful.) [Amatuka]
related_entries.annotation_html: kudasai    (なさい and ください can both be used to make requests, although なさい is probably more forceful.) [Amatuka]
